entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Takes a session and a user_id and writes deleted_at on the users row.

stores.name: users

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: The column the close_account route writes and the purge job filters on.

erasure.note: close_account only sets deleted_at; the celery beat task purge_closed_accounts calls session.delete on users rows whose deleted_at is older than RETENTION_DAYS.

stores.note: Table holding the account holder's email and name.

stores.name: invoices

fields.name: reference
fields.note: A comment on this line says the value is kept for the statutory accounting period and that the purge job does not touch this table.

erasure.note: The User.invoices relationship carries no cascade string, so the ORM delete does not propagate; the only deletion path is the foreign key's ondelete=CASCADE, and the engine URL is SQLite with no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON connect listener in the repository, so foreign key enforcement is not shown.

stores.note: Table of invoice rows carrying a user_id foreign key to users.

stores.name: nightly_backup

fields.name: email
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row with getattr.

fields.name: full_name
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row with getattr.

fields.name: reference
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each Invoice row with getattr.

erasure.note: dump_database writes a JSON file of users and invoices rows; the module carries a cron SCHEDULE and BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS = 35, and no code in the repository deletes the file.

stores.note: JSON file written by dump_database from the users and invoices tables.

retention.criteria: rows whose deleted_at is older than the cutoff are deleted by the nightly purge task
